6.5.goal: Check whether the average nitrate level in a river differs from the 3.2 mg/L guideline, using the lesson's nine readings.

blocks.title: Enter the data
blocks.text: Nine nitrate readings from one river, in mg/L, and the guideline value we want to compare against. NumPy holds the numbers and SciPy supplies the test.
blocks.code:
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

nitrate = np.array([3.1, 4.2, 2.8, 3.9, 4.5, 3.3, 4.1, 3.7, 3.5])
guideline = 3.2

print('readings:', len(nitrate))

blocks.title: Describe the sample
blocks.text: Always look at the numbers before testing them. The mean is the sample's centre, the standard deviation (ddof=1, the sample version) is its typical spread, and the standard error says how much a mean of 9 readings wobbles.
blocks.code:
mean = nitrate.mean()
sd = nitrate.std(ddof=1)
se = sd / np.sqrt(len(nitrate))

print(f'mean = {mean:.3f}')
print(f'sd   = {sd:.3f}')
print(f'se   = {se:.3f}')

blocks.title: Run the one-sample t-test
blocks.text: ttest_1samp asks: if the true average were exactly 3.2, how surprising is a sample mean this far away? It returns the t statistic (distance in standard errors) and the two-sided p-value.
blocks.code:
result = stats.ttest_1samp(nitrate, popmean=guideline)

print(f't  = {result.statistic:.3f}')
print(f'df = {len(nitrate) - 1}')
print(f'p  = {result.pvalue:.4f}')

blocks.title: Add a confidence interval
blocks.text: A 95% interval shows the range of true averages that fit the data. The guideline sits outside it, which agrees with the small p-value.
blocks.code:
ci = result.confidence_interval(confidence_level=0.95)

print(f'95% CI: ({ci.low:.3f}, {ci.high:.3f})')
print('guideline inside the interval?', ci.low <= guideline <= ci.high)

r.expect: t = 2.5866, df = 8, p-value = 0.03226; 95 percent confidence interval: 3.252 to 4.104; sample mean 3.678
r.note: t.test prints the t statistic, degrees of freedom, p-value and the 95% confidence interval together.

spss.menu: Analyze > Compare Means > One-Sample T Test
spss.syntax:
DATA LIST FREE / nitrate.
BEGIN DATA
3.1 4.2 2.8 3.9 4.5 3.3 4.1 3.7 3.5
END DATA.
T-TEST
  /TESTVAL=3.2
  /VARIABLES=nitrate
  /CRITERIA=CI(.95).
spss.note: In the One-Sample Test table read t, df and Sig. (2-tailed); the confidence interval is for the difference from 3.2.

stata.code:
clear
input nitrate
3.1
4.2
2.8
3.9
4.5
3.3
4.1
3.7
3.5
end
ttest nitrate == 3.2
stata.note: ttest reports the mean, its 95% confidence interval, t, degrees of freedom and the two-sided p-value (the middle Pr(|T| > |t|) line).
